notes: SHIP v1.14.428 - THE ALERT TOKEN IS DECLARED, AND THREE DEAD DECLARATIONS COME BACK TO LIFE. WHAT WAS WRONG. --alert was referenced but declared NOWHERE, and an undefined var() invalidates its ENTIRE declaration in silence. Three rules set color: var(--alert) with no fallback and therefore painted nothing at all: .bd-pri-btn.active[data-pri=P1] at :3838, .bd-pri-tag.P1 at :3840 and .bd-sla.overdue at :3844. A P1 priority tag and an OVERDUE SLA inherited whatever colour surrounded them, so the attention channel was absent on exactly the two states that exist to shout. Two other uses were always fine because they carry a fallback - #storage-warn at :13586 and #offline-banner at :13590 both write var(--alert,#ff3b3b) - and that fallback is also the proof of what the value was meant to be. THE FIX IS ONE DECLARATION. --alert: #ff3b3b on :root. This is NOT a new design decision: it adopts the value the author had already written twice, so the two banners that already worked are byte-identical and only the three dead rules change. Deliberately NOT folded into --red (#ff453a) - that is a different red, and unifying them would be a design ruling rather than a defect fix. EXACT PRECEDENT, ONE LINE ABOVE IT. --teal carries a comment recording the identical failure: undefined on :root, so var(--teal) in #pg-cmd .tile.hot-teal and the shared card was invalid and the glass housing collapsed once a scan ran. Same class, same fix, now with a gate behind it. HOW IT WAS FOUND, WHICH MATTERS MORE THAN THE FIX. Not by eye - by a new gate, spec 19-design-tokens-and-picker, written while automating BATCH-VERIFY item 9 under the owner ruling that the owner is not the test harness. It walks every CSS rule, collects every custom property DECLARED and every one REFERENCED, and reports names that are referenced with no fallback, declared in no stylesheet, set on no element and never written by setProperty. Nothing else in this project can see that failure: brace balance passes, node --check never reads CSS, and the CSS parser reports nothing. v1.14.237 shipped exactly this class for two versions when a comment containing a slash-star-slash sequence closed early and swallowed the whole #forge3d-sheet token block. THREE PROBE BUGS WERE FIXED BEFORE THE GATE COULD BE TRUSTED, each of which made it look green while proving almost nothing: a per-sheet try/catch let a single bad rule abandon the rest of its stylesheet, so it reported 2 tokens where there are 210; var(--x, fallback) was counted as a defect when it degrades by design; and tokens written at runtime through setProperty are genuinely declared but invisible to a CSSOM walk. A gate that under-reports is worse than no gate. The finding was PINNED as an exact expected list rather than skipped, reported to the owner, and only fixed on his word because colour sits under the design-system lock. The pin is now removed and the assertion is back to EMPTY, so any dead token is a failure from here on. TESTS: 19 (3) and 06-composition (12) green - 15 passed. GATES: 3 inline blocks compile, node --check sw.js, valid JSON, CSS braces 4583/4583, CRLF 56959 with 0 bare LF, three-stamp lockstep. No layout change, no logic change, no parser change. ?legacy=1 unaffected - the token sits on :root and the three revived rules are legacy-house selectors that were already there and already intended to be red. DEVICE-VERIFY: none required. This is a colour restored to three text states, provable in the harness; the owner sees it in normal use.
